background.summary: The reader has finished an undergraduate computer science degree: asymptotic analysis, basic algorithms (divide and conquer, sorting, recurrences, schoolbook integer arithmetic), discrete mathematics, and introductory linear algebra, abstract algebra (groups, rings, fields, modular arithmetic) and probability. They know Turing machines and tapes at a basic level, but not the multitape fixed-alphabet cost model in detail, nor Fourier-analytic multiplication, FFT variants, or specialist algebra such as bilinear forms over F_2 and matrix factorizations like Bruhat.
